_meta.anti_fabrication_note: Protocol equations from Needham-Schroeder 1978 CACM pp.993-999. The replay attack on this protocol was identified by Denning and Sacco 1981 CACM pp.533-536 and elaborated in BAN 1990 TOCS pp.18-36. Page numbers marked REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION must be confirmed against the original PDFs.
_meta.primary_source: Needham, R.M.; Schroeder, M.D. Using Encryption for Authentication in Large Networks of Computers. CACM 21(12):993-999, 1978. DOI:10.1145/359657.359659
_meta.attack_source: Denning, D.E.; Sacco, G.M. Timestamps in Key Distribution Protocols. CACM 24(8):533-536, 1981. DOI:10.1145/358722.358740

equation_source_page: REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION — equations for NSSK appear in Needham-Schroeder 1978 p.993; Denning-Sacco 1981 cites the protocol and demonstrates the attack
attack_source_page: REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION — confirm exact page of attack within Denning-Sacco 1981 pp.533-536
cryptographic_parameters: Symmetric encryption (generic; DES assumed in practice era). K_AS = long-term key between A and server S. K_BS = long-term key between B and server S. K_AB = session key generated by S. Nonces Na (from A), Nb (from B).
original_equations:
A → S : A, B, Na
S → A : {Na, B, K_AB, {K_AB, A}K_BS}K_AS
A → B : {K_AB, A}K_BS
B → A : {Nb}K_AB
A → B : {Nb - 1}K_AB

normalized_equations.description: A requests a session key for communicating with B, sending both identities and a nonce Na.
Server returns: A's nonce (freshness proof), B's name, the session key K_AB, and a ticket for B. All encrypted under A's long-term key K_AS.
A forwards the ticket to B. B decrypts with K_BS and learns K_AB and A's identity.
B generates nonce Nb and sends a challenge to A encrypted under the session key K_AB.
A decrypts the challenge, computes Nb-1 (or f(Nb)), and responds. This proves A holds K_AB.

attacker_identity: outsider — has previously compromised an old session key K_AB_old
attack_name: Denning-Sacco Ticket Replay Attack on NSSK
attack_trace:
Precondition: E has stored a ticket from a previous session: {K_AB_old, A}K_BS and has since learned K_AB_old.

Step 1: E → B  : {K_AB_old, A}K_BS
         E replays the old ticket to B, pretending to be A.
Step 2: B → E  : {Nb}K_AB_old
         B sends a challenge encrypted under K_AB_old, believing it is speaking to A.
Step 3: E → B  : {Nb - 1}K_AB_old
         E decrypts the challenge using the known K_AB_old and responds correctly.
Outcome: B believes it has freshly established a session with A under session key K_AB_old. In reality, B holds a stale key that E also knows. All subsequent session traffic encrypted under K_AB_old is readable by E.
security_violation: The ticket {K_AB, A}K_BS contains no timestamp and no nonce from B. B cannot determine whether the ticket was freshly issued by S or is being replayed from a previous session. An attacker who learns an old session key can replay its ticket to B indefinitely until B's long-term key K_BS changes.
verified_by: REQUIRES_MANUAL_VERIFICATION — confirm equation page (NSSK in NS 1978) and attack page (Denning-Sacco 1981) against original PDFs
notes: Protocol equations: Needham-Schroeder 1978 CACM p.993. Attack identification: Denning-Sacco 1981 CACM pp.533-536. Also discussed in BAN 1990 ACM TOCS 8(1):18-36 Section 4.4. The Nb-1 convention in step 5 may vary: some papers use f(Nb) or {Nb, 1}K_AB — confirm against original. Fix: add timestamp T to ticket to become {K_AB, A, T}K_BS (Denning-Sacco 1981 proposal).
